newsitem.title: UK: SOCCER-BARCELONA GO TOP WITH FIVE-GOAL AWAY SPREE.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER-BARCELONA GO TOP WITH FIVE-GOAL AWAY SPREE.

text.p: Barcelona and Juventus both moved to the top of their leagues at the weekend but the Spaniards did it the hard way, fighting back from 3-1 down to snatch a thrilling and controversial 5-3 win away to Real Zaragoza.
Spain
The Real Zaragoza-Barcelona match turned on a disputed penalty decision 17 minutes from time when Zaragoza led 3-2, a linesman alerting the referee to an infringement in the home side's penalty area.

The referee sent off Zaragoza's Xavier Aguado, Barcelona scored from the spot and then romped to a victory which took them two points clear of Deportivo Coruna and Real Madrid, Brazilian Ronaldo getting two goals on the way.
Real Madris won 3-2 in Oviedo while Deportivo beat previous leaders Real Betis 2-1.
Italy

League leaders Parma lost 2-1 at Lazio allowing European champions Juventus to leapfrog to the top with a 1-0 victory over Fiorentina thanks to a Michele Padovano goal after eight minutes. The win was marred by the sending off of Croat striker Alen Boksic for elbowing Portugal's Rui Costa in the face.

Title-holders AC Milan moved up to second with a 3-0 thrashing of Perugia, Liberia's George Weah scoring twice and Roberto Baggio adding a third. Milan's last two goals came after Croatian midfielder Zvonimir Boban had been sent off in the 67th minute.
Juventus lead with 10 points, one ahead of AC Milan with Internazionale third on eight.
England
Liverpool stayed three points clear after goals from Stan Collymore and Michael Thomas secured a 2-1 win at West Ham, their seventh successive win in all competitions.

Champions Manchester United also kept their unbeaten record with a comfortable 2-0 victory over Spurs, both goals coming from Norwegian striker Ole Gunnar Solskjaer, to move into third place a point behind Arsenal who beat Sunderland 2-0 at home.
Liverpool are top with 20 points from eight games followed by Arsenal on 17 and Manchester United on 16. Newcastle United, fifth on 15, would move second if they beat Aston Villa on Monday.
Germany
Midfielder Andreas Herzog took sweet revenge on his former team mates at Bayern Munich, scoring twice in Werder Bremen's 3-0 win to knock the 13 times champions off the top.

Challengers VfB Stuttgart seized their chance to go first with alacrity, returning to their stylish winning ways with a 5-2 away win over Bayern's local rivals 1860 Munich featuring two goals from Brazilian Giovane Elber.
Stuttgart lead on 19 points, one ahead of Bayer Leverkusen and two in front of Bayern. Champions Borussia Dortmund beat St Pauli 2-1 to go fifth on 16 points.
France

They were no changes at the top with leaders Paris St Germain coming from 2-0 down to draw 2-2 in Guingamp, conceding their first goals of the season, and main rivals Bastia and Bordeaux also forced to settle for a single point.
Bordeaux striker Jean-Pierre Papin returned to play in Marseille for the first time since he left the Mediterranean port four years ago but failed to get on the scoresheet in a goalless draw.
With PSG in command on 21 points, Bastia retained second place on 18 points thanks to a 2-2 draw at bottom-of-the-table Nancy. Bordeaux are third on 17.
Netherlands
Leaders Feyenoord stumbled to their first defeat of the season, going down 4-2 away to Vitesse Arnhem but stayed top by two points as PSV Eindhoven could only draw 2-2 in Utrecht.
Ajax Amsterdam continued their poor run, drawing 1-1 to Twente in Enschede, and are ninth with only six goals scored in eight games.
Portugal

Reigning champions Porto were held to a 0-0 draw at home by lowly Estrela Amadora and lost Brazilian defender Luis "Lula" Marcos with a suspected broken leg. Sporting Lisbon, 1-0 winners away to Leca, took a two-point lead at the top. Benfica are three behind them but with a game in hand.
Belgium
Standard Liege stayed top with a 3-1 home win over Mechelen but champions Club Brugge remained level on points after beating Germinal Ekeren 2-0.
Scotland
Rangers took a big step towards equalling Celtic's record of nine successive titles when they beat their Glasgow rivals 2-0 to move five points clear.
